      <title>Fears grow that US will impose sanctions on ICJ judges ahead of Myanmar genocide ruling</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/us-sanctions-icj-judges-myanmar-genocide-ruling-israel-gaza-court</link>
      <description><p>A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza</p><p>Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize">Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay</a>, if the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/15/myanmar-rohingya-genocide-icj">court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide</a> against the Rohingya.</p><p>The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/us-sanctions-icj-judges-myanmar-genocide-ruling-israel-gaza-court">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans</link>
      <description><p>Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans</p><p>The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.</p><p>The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/mar/17/egypt-eu-deal-refugees-mediterranean">promised by Ursula von der Leyen</a>, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda</link>
      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:10:46 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>French interior minister accused of 'exaggerating' police protest injury figures</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-french-interior-minister-accused-of-exaggerating-police-protest-injury-figures</link><description>
A group of lawyers have called for an investigation into French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez who they accuse of "spreading false information" about the number of injuries suffered by law enforcement officers since the start of the current protest movement, which they say was used "to justify a disproportionate use of force" against high school protesters.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">294b16e6-e335-11f1-af18-6757e9484dfb</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:09:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg">AFP - SEBASTIEN BOZON</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'We weren't afraid of the future': France's student protests today and in May '68</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-we-weren-t-afraid-of-the-future-france-s-student-protests-today-and-in-may-68</link><description>
As students across France continue demonstrating against conditions in schools, the movement has drawn inevitable comparisons with the biggest student protests in the country's history – those of May 1968. While this date remains a rallying cry for many young French people, they are calling for change in a world that has altered profoundly in the past 58 years.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">457488e8-dceb-11f1-88f8-bd68fc553891</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:01:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg">© JACQUES MARIE / AFP </source><dc:creator>Jessica Phelan</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Lower turnout at latest French cost-of-living protests, but anger still raw</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-lower-turnout-at-latest-french-cost-of-living-protests-but-anger-still-raw</link><description>
Tens of thousands of people demonstrated across France on Tuesday in a fresh nationwide public sector strike over pay and the cost of living. Although turnout was lower than at previous protests, anger remained strong – with many demonstrators also voicing fears about the far right coming to power in the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5222ba24-e2a9-11f1-8d87-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T145907Z-1351244212-RC2QPOAW8GVH-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5222ba24-e2a9-11f1-8d87-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T145907Z-1351244212-RC2QPOAW8GVH-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2b33b0b8-e32a-11f1-9717-657339b41114</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:50:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5222ba24-e2a9-11f1-8d87-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T145907Z-1351244212-RC2QPOAW8GVH-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Gonzalo Fuentes</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>EU economics chief warns France and Belgium must reduce deficit and public debt</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-eu-economics-chief-warns-france-and-belgium-must-reduce-deficit-and-public-debt</link><description>
France and Belgium must bring down their public debt and deficit levels, European Union economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis warned on Tuesday as he unveiled the European Commission's autumn economic forecast. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">065f0570-e281-11f1-84fb-2734eec1674a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:00:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg">REUTERS - Yves Herman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'A message to drug gangs': life sentences for 'barbaric' Marseille murders</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-a-message-to-drug-gangs-life-sentences-for-barbaric-marseille-murders</link><description>
Two leading figures in Marseille's drug-trafficking underworld were sentenced to life imprisonment on Monday for a triple murder in 2020. Anti-drugs activist Amine Kessaci, whose brother was among the victims, hailed the verdict as a "message to the narcocracy".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1288fd3c-e282-11f1-91a0-f16e280f34ca</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:59:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg">AFP - THIBAUD MORITZ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French presidential candidates clash over tax, housing and the minimum wage</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-french-presidential-candidates-clash-over-tax-housing-and-the-minimum-wage</link><description>
Five candidates for the 2027 French presidential election on Monday evening wrangled over issues including the cost of living crisis, the minimum wage and single parents in a live televised debate.

French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description><p>Company issues first earnings report after ouster of CEO over allegations of affair with suspected Chinese spy</p><p>Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, the chairman of the company’s board said Tuesday. Harvey Jones made the remark during Nvidia’s first quarterly earnings report since Jensen Huang’s ouster.</p><p>Nvidia announced the same day that its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming in at $115.84bn, doubling from the same time period a year ago.       <description><p>International investigation using trove of leaked internal data allegedly shows German bank overlooked compliance concerns to safeguard profits</p><p>Deutsche Bank reportedly dismissed warnings about its dealings with risky clients, including high-profile Russian oligarchs, to protect profits, the findings of an investigation into a trove of leaked bank documents indicate.</p><p>A leak of 15m internal files is reported to show that the troubled German bank repeatedly ignored concerns by its compliance officers about its risk-taking, despite having already <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2019/apr/17/deutsche-bank-faces-action-over-20bn-russian-money-laundering-scheme">been caught being used to launder billions of dollars</a> for Russian criminals, spies and oligarchs between 2010 and 2015.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/deutsche-bank-dimissed-warnings-risky-clients-reports-claim">Continue reading...</a></description>

Goodbye to a steel monstrosity seemingly designed by a five-year-old</p><p>Elon Musk is having a rough go of it, isn’t he? The world’s richest man spent almost half a billion dollars on the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/04/elon-musk-midterm-spending-analysis">midterms</a> in a failed attempt to defend Republican control of government. Now the tech mogul, who moved from California to Texas to escape Democrats and regulations, finds himself in a newly blue state. He also finds himself the subject of an unflattering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/musk-review-epic-study-worlds-richest-most-banal-man-elon-film">documentary</a> and, if the Democrats follow through on threats to investigate him, could potentially be in a spot of legal bother.</p><p>And to top it all off? Musk’s beloved Cybertruck, the steel monstrosity that looks as if it were designed by a five-year-old, is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/06/tesla-to-wind-down-cybertruck-production-as-elon-musk-focuses-on-robotics-and-ai">winding down production</a>. According to Musk, this isn’t because it’s an abject failure, but because he is channelling his energy into other things. “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” Musk <a href="https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2119691615774146614?a=pN3ISFVZZ-aU4_-TlJw&amp;s=20">tweeted</a> on Monday. “But rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” (The Cybercab is a two-passenger robotaxi.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/netflix-fox-2030-world-cup-television-rights</link>
      <description><p>The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry</p><p>The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.</p><p>Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/netflix-fox-2030-world-cup-television-rights">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘When I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West’: the two lives of Bromley footballer Omar Sowunmi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/omar-sowunmi-bromley-footballer-model-kanye-west</link>
      <description><p>Full-time defender and part-time model, the 31-year-old is happy to shine a light on both sides of his dual career</p><p>“I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi says. He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds.</p><p>Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their new manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/omar-sowunmi-bromley-footballer-model-kanye-west">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/premier-league-teams-full-backs-opta-analyst</link>
      <description><p>The role of full-back has changed massively in recent years. We analyse how all 20 sides are approaching the position</p><p>By <a href="https://theanalyst.com/">Opta Analyst</a></p><p>Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted.</p><p>Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you’ve got to be a centre-midfielder, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/premier-league-teams-full-backs-opta-analyst">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/biggest-leaps-across-fifa-football-rankings-the-knowledge</link>
      <description><p>Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more</p><ul><li><p><a href="mailto:knowledge@theguardian.com"><strong>Mail us</strong></a><strong> with all of your questions and answers</strong></p></li></ul><p><strong>“The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,”</strong> writes Bogdan Kotarlic. <strong>“Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?”</strong></p><p>The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: <strong>Wales</strong> from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chris Coleman, <strong>Northern Ireland</strong> from 129th in 2004 to 20th in 2017.</p><p><strong>183 places</strong> Montenegro (16th/199th)</p><p><strong>165</strong> Kuwait (24/189)</p><p><strong>160</strong> Bosnia and Herzegovina (13/173)</p><p><strong>155</strong> Cape Verde (27/182)</p><p><strong>153</strong> Central African Republic (49/202)</p><p><strong>151</strong> Libya (36/187)</p><p><strong>146</strong> Equatorial Guinea (49/195)</p><p><strong>144</strong> Moldova (37/181)</p><p><strong>141</strong> El Salvador (49/190)</p><p><strong>136</strong> Cuba (46/182), Slovakia (14/150)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/biggest-leaps-across-fifa-football-rankings-the-knowledge">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Jack Grealish recalls a golden age of mavericks – but football has moved on</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/jack-grealish-recalls-a-golden-age-of-mavericks-but-football-has-moved-on</link>
      <description><p>Everton forward has magical talent and popularity to burn, but has come up against hard reality of the modern game</p><p>Thomas Tuchel has never called up the player he once claimed to love “everything about”. The reason for Jack Grealish’s omission from Tuchel’s first England squad in March 2025 was given as “he simply has no rhythm”.</p><p>Catch a falling star? Grealish <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/29/jack-grealish-axed-everton-breach-club-discipline-newcastle-caraboao-cup">was suspended by Everton</a> for three matches following “a breach of club discipline”. Suggestions his loan from Manchester City might be cancelled were calmed by David Moyes. Last week, Grealish played in a behind-closed doors friendly against Derby before issuing an Instagram statement: “I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.” Amid tabloid tales of karaoke nights and extended socialising, how close is the former boy wonder, now 31, to blowing it?</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/jack-grealish-recalls-a-golden-age-of-mavericks-but-football-has-moved-on">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/fifa-hydration-breaks-2030-world-cup-tv-right-documents</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Controversial breaks were financial boon for broadcasters</p></li><li><p>Fifa flags possible benefits but says no decision made</p></li></ul><p>Fifa’s tender documents for TV rights for the 2030 World Cup includes a provision for broadcasters<strong> </strong>to sell adverts during hydration breaks in a strong indication <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/26/fifa-unites-the-world-in-anger-at-hydration-breaks-aka-ad-breaks">the controversial stoppages</a> will be retained.</p><p>A three-minute break midway through each half was introduced for the first time at all 104 matches at last summer’s World Cup in the interests of player welfare, a radical move that also provided a commercial boon for broadcasters, particularly the rights holders in the United States, Fox Sports and Telemundo.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/fifa-hydration-breaks-2030-world-cup-tv-right-documents">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>Haaland’s late penalty grabs Norway last-eight spot</p></li><li><p>Parrott penalties help Republic of Ireland secure playoff</p></li></ul><p>A wonder strike from Justin Devenny earned <strong>Northern Ireland </strong>top spot in Nations League Group B2 and promotion to the top tier of the competition.       <title>‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/pfa-maheta-molango-interview-fifa-gianni-infantino-interview</link>
      <description><p>At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’</p><p>After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 43-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.”</p><p>In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4m) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the English players’ union observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/pfa-maheta-molango-interview-fifa-gianni-infantino-interview">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/janine-van-wyck-south-africa-wafcon-book-extract-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter</link>
      <description><p>In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations</p><p>I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group.</p><p>As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/janine-van-wyck-south-africa-wafcon-book-extract-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Portugal’s new No 7 Forbs channels Ronaldo for winner as Wales are denied</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wales-portugal-nations-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese Football Federation put it. A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards.</p><p>For Wales, a Nations League relegation playoff double-header awaits in March, with Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia and Herzegovina – who knocked them out of World Cup qualifying this year – all potential opponents in Friday’s draw in Switzerland. Afterwards Craig Bellamy stressed the importance of keeping elite company to accelerate improvement but reiterated that he will not be in the job beyond Euro 2028, after which his contract expires.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wales-portugal-nations-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation</p><p>“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes.</p><p>The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/14/diego-maradona-argentina-world-cup">Argentina’s football folklore</a> are spliced with excellent archive material.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/reliving-the-drama-england-and-argentina-stars-watch-1986-classic-with-fresh-eyes">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland</link>
      <description><p>The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job</p><p>The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments.</p><p>There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/switzerland-scotland-nations-league-match-report">4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland</a> was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Danny Kelly obituary</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/17/danny-kelly-obituary</link>
      <description><p>Ebullient journalist, magazine editor and broadcaster whose passion for music and football shone through all his work</p><p>Danny Kelly, who has died aged 69, influenced music journalism and sports broadcasting for more than four decades. Humour, enthusiasm and encyclopedic knowledge were the hallmarks of his work as a writer and editor at the New Musical Express (NME) and Q magazine, and throughout his online, TV and audio career, most prominently around his passion for football.</p><p>In 1997 Kelly helped set up Football 365, one of the earliest football websites, and still one of the most popular in the UK. He hosted radio shows on BBC 5 Live, TalkSport, BT Sport and Times Radio, as well as many podcasts including The View from the Lane, about the team he had supported since childhood, Tottenham Hotspur.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/17/danny-kelly-obituary">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham</link>
      <description><p>Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France </p><p>There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling.</p><p>Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/nov/04/slavia-prague-arsenal-champions-league-match-report">at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days</a>, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/mar/14/arsenal-everton-premier-league-match-report">Premier League’s youngest goalscorer</a>. He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Echoes of Azteca but not like Argentina: fearless England start afresh in Madrid</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/azteca-argentina-fearless-england-start-afresh-spain</link>
      <description><p>‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics</p><p>Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">won 3-2</a>. The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before.</p><p>The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he said, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/06/england-mexico-match-report-jude-bellingham-harry-kane-world-cup">win at the Azteca Stadium</a> and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/azteca-argentina-fearless-england-start-afresh-spain">Continue reading...</a></description>

Le « résultat de plusieurs mois de travail », pour Joseph Henrotin, chercheur spécialisé dans la défense et rédacteur en chef de la revue spécialisée « DSI ».]]></description><guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.lemonde.fr/international/video/2026/11/18/guerre-en-ukraine-pourquoi-l-armee-ukrainienne-a-vise-ce-pont-strategique-en-crimee_6813095_3210.html</guid><link>https://www.lemonde.fr/international/video/2026/11/18/guerre-en-ukraine-pourquoi-l-armee-ukrainienne-a-vise-ce-pont-strategique-en-crimee_6813095_3210.html</link><media:content width="644" height="322" url="https://img.lemde.fr/2026/11/17/94/0/3008/1504/644/322/60/0/17a8cb2_ftp-1-ew8uoigr2ni3-2026-11-17t132708z-465711953-rc2ppoaqenqs-rtrmadp-3-ukraine-crisis-attack-crimea-sbu.JPG"><media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">SERVICE DE SECURITE UKRAINIEN/REUTERS</media:credit></media:content></item><item><title><![CDATA[La Suède refuse l’asile à l’ancien ambassadeur d’Afghanistan]]></title><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:17:44 +0100</pubDate><updated>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:10:10 +0100</updated><description><![CDATA[En poste depuis 2019 à Stockholm, le réformiste Abbas Noyan, qui n’a jamais reconnu le régime des talibans, a perdu son accréditation fin 2024. Aujourd’hui, la Suède entend l’expulser aux Etats-Unis où il a vécu quelques années au début des années 2000.]]></description><guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.lemonde.fr/international/article/2026/11/18/la-suede-refuse-l-asile-a-l-ancien-ambassadeur-d-afghanistan_6813092_3210.html</guid><link>https://www.lemonde.fr/international/article/2026/11/18/la-suede-refuse-l-asile-a-l-ancien-ambassadeur-d-afghanistan_6813092_3210.html</link><media:content width="644" height="322" url="https://img.lemde.fr/2026/11/17/320/0/3840/1920/644/322/60/0/a64be57_upload-1-qelb7qrqtdwn-3840px-abbas-noyan-at-campaign.jpg"><media:description type="plain">Abbas Noyan (à gauche), lors d’une réunion de campagne à Kaboul, en octobre 2018.</media:description><media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Fara Abbas/CC BY-SA 4.0</media:credit></media:content></item><item><title><![CDATA[Nvidia : l’affaire Jensen Huang révèle les failles de l’administration Trump sur la Chine]]></title><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:30:14 +0100</pubDate><updated>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:17:49 +0100</updated><description><![CDATA[Soutenu par la Silicon Valley et d’excellents résultats, le fondateur de la firme de microprocesseurs, rattrapé par plusieurs affaires d’adultère, tente de reprendre la tête de l’entreprise, qu’il avait été contraint de quitter le 12 novembre. Les partisans de Donald Trump dénoncent les zones obscures de l’affaire.]]></description><guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2026/11/18/nvidia-l-affaire-jensen-huang-revele-les-failles-de-l-administration-trump-sur-la-chine_6813087_3234.html</guid><link>https://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2026/11/18/nvidia-l-affaire-jensen-huang-revele-les-failles-de-l-administration-trump-sur-la-chine_6813087_3234.html</link><media:content width="644" height="322" url="https://img.lemde.fr/2026/11/17/596/0/5392/2696/644/322/60/0/9e5ce8e_ftp-1-hxs6l82xi455-afp-d7rp3g3.jpg"><media:description type="plain">Jensen Huang, à Berlin, le 21 octobre 2026. </media:description><media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">JOHN MACDOUGALL/AFP</media:credit></media:content></item></channel></rss>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title>L'actualité économique et politique en Europe - RFI</title><description>Suivez l'actualité en direct dédiée au continent Européen - Les derniers reportages, news et informations en continu en Europe, Emissions, Podcast, dossiers sur RFI.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/</link><lastBuildDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:41:43 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Europe</category><title>L'UE propose un nouveau prêt de 45 milliards d'euros à l'Ukraine pour 2027</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261118-l-ue-propose-un-nouveau-pr%C3%AAt-de-45-milliards-d-euros-%C3%A0-l-ukraine-pour-2027</link><description>
La Commission européenne va proposer aux Vingt-Sept d'accorder un nouveau prêt d'un montant de 45 milliards d'euros à l'Ukraine, pour combler son déficit budgétaire en 2027, a annoncé mercredi 18 novembre sa présidente Ursula von der Leyen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/600fd41c-e346-11f1-9cf3-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26322388827717.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/600fd41c-e346-11f1-9cf3-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26322388827717.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">aa5ff79a-e346-11f1-887b-45ebcb86156e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:10:45 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/600fd41c-e346-11f1-9cf3-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26322388827717.jpg">© Omar Havana / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Appels sur l'actualité</category><title>Fifa : Philippe Diallo peut-il battre Gianni Infantino à la présidence?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/appels-sur-l-actualit%C3%A9/20261118-fifa-philippe-diallo-peut-il-battre-gianni-infantino-%C3%A0-la-pr%C3%A9sidence</link><description>
Le président de la Fédération française de football, Philippe Diallo, a été choisi par l’UEFA pour affronter Gianni Infantino lors de l’élection à la présidence de la Fifa, le 18 mars 2027 prochain, à Rabat. L’instance européenne, qui lui apporte son soutien unanime, cherche à proposer une autre voie après ses désaccords avec le président sortant. Pourquoi le choix de l'UEFA s'est-il finalement porté sur Philippe Diallo pour affronter Gianni Infantino ? Même si le président de la FFF a le soutien unanime de l’UEFA, le président sortant bénéficie notamment de celui de la CAF. Comment peut-il convaincre les fédérations africaines à voter pour lui ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2918a058-68b0-11f1-9902-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP24349559957256.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2918a058-68b0-11f1-9902-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP24349559957256.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8bb060bc-e285-11f1-9d3c-c5ab8ff84d6a</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:10:52 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Namouri Dosso</dc:creator></item><item><category>Appels sur l'actualité</category><title>« Hubs de retour » : pourquoi les Européens misent sur le Rwanda?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/appels-sur-l-actualit%C3%A9/20261118-hubs-de-retour-pourquoi-les-europ%C3%A9ens-misent-sur-le-rwanda</link><description>
Cinq pays européens, l’Allemagne, l’Autriche, le Danemark, la Grèce et les Pays-Bas, veulent ouvrir au Rwanda, en 2027, un premier « hub de retour » destiné à des personnes dont la demande d’asile a été rejetée et qui ne peuvent pas être renvoyées dans leur pays d’origine. Que sait-on exactement de ce projet ? Pourquoi le Rwanda en est-il le principal pays partenaire ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/013e2372-e1d3-11f1-80e8-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320558302536.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/013e2372-e1d3-11f1-80e8-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320558302536.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d0fed750-e26e-11f1-bbb4-8dbca557f2ff</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:05:52 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Namouri Dosso</dc:creator></item><item><category>Appels sur l'actualité</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine : une adhésion à l’Otan contre un retrait du Donbass?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/appels-sur-l-actualit%C3%A9/20261118-guerre-en-ukraine-une-adh%C3%A9sion-%C3%A0-l-otan-contre-un-retrait-du-donbass</link><description>
Le Donbass contre une adhésion à l’Otan ? Selon Volodymyr Zelensky, les négociateurs américains ont évoqué pour la première fois cette hypothèse auprès de Kiev, après les pourparlers d’Abou Dhabi. Elle placerait au cœur d’un éventuel accord de paix deux questions parmi les plus sensibles du conflit : le contrôle du territoire ukrainien et les garanties de sécurité réclamées par Kiev. Une telle idée est-elle actuellement plausible ? Qu’en pensent les Ukrainiens ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a1f041c8-b62d-11f1-825e-1d61c7110e09/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26189492545041-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a1f041c8-b62d-11f1-825e-1d61c7110e09/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26189492545041-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">03c94064-e28b-11f1-b59d-b13fcfeca3d3</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:00:53 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Namouri Dosso</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine: en Crimée ou à Kiev, les frappes contre des ponts perturbent la logistique et le quotidien</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261118-guerre-en-ukraine-en-crim%C3%A9e-ou-%C3%A0-kiev-les-frappes-contre-des-ponts-perturbent-la-logistique-et-le-quotidien</link><description>
En début de semaine, la Russie et l'Ukraine ont à nouveau multiplié les frappes. L'Ukraine a frappé le pont de Kertch, en Crimée, causant d'importants dégâts à cette infrastructure importante pour le ravitaillement russe. De son côté, la Russie a mené plusieurs attaques contre des ponts à Kiev, rendant ainsi la vie difficile dans la capitale ukrainienne.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/94298844-e312-11f1-acd6-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321401562180.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/94298844-e312-11f1-acd6-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321401562180.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c9b65388-e313-11f1-a76c-1fbd63ebc9be</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 06:08:19 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/94298844-e312-11f1-acd6-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321401562180.jpg">© Evgeniy Maloletka / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Allemagne: la Deutsche Bank au cœur d'un nouveau scandale de pratiques douteuses</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-allemagne-la-deutsche-bank-au-c%C5%93ur-d-un-nouveau-scandale-de-pratiques-douteuses</link><description>
La plus grande institution bancaire allemande fait une nouvelle fois la une de la presse, mardi 17 novembre 2026. Une fuite de 15 millions de documents lève le voile sur ses pratiques douteuses et la manière dont la Deutsche Bank a protégé ses clients les plus sulfureux, comme le pédocriminel américain Jeffrey Epstein.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bf6972a8-e2a4-11f1-8961-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/ALLEMAGNE-BERLIN-DEUTSCHE-BANK.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bf6972a8-e2a4-11f1-8961-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/ALLEMAGNE-BERLIN-DEUTSCHE-BANK.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d113dcd2-e2a4-11f1-9635-7d42f883cc1b</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:35:05 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bf6972a8-e2a4-11f1-8961-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/ALLEMAGNE-BERLIN-DEUTSCHE-BANK.jpg">REUTERS - Nadja Wohlleben</source><dc:creator>Nathanaël Vittrant</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Projet de «hub de retour»: «On n'a aucune idée de la manière dont le Rwanda va traiter ces étrangers»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261117-projet-de-hub-de-retour-on-n-a-aucune-id%C3%A9e-de-la-mani%C3%A8re-dont-le-rwanda-va-traiter-ces-%C3%A9trangers</link><description>
« Ni avenir, ni humanité dans le projet de centre de migrants au Rwanda » : ce sont les mots du Premier ministre espagnol, Pedro Sanchez, face à l'initiative détaillée, lundi 16 novembre, par cinq pays de l'Union européenne, dont l'Allemagne et le Danemark, d'ouvrir dans ce pays le tout premier centre pour des migrants expulsés d'Europe. Les promoteurs du projet assurent vouloir créer un centre ouvert, où les migrants seront accompagnés et pourront bénéficier de programmes de formation, d'accès à l’emploi, ainsi qu'à l'éducation et à des centres de santé. Assiste-t-on à un tournant dans le durcissement de l'Europe en matière d'immigration ? L'analyse d'Antoine Pecoud, professeur de sociologie à l'université de Sorbonne Paris-Nord et directeur du département Policy de l'Institut des migrations. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4f886fa4-a8eb-11f1-80af-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-04T160250Z-834668253-RC2CCNAR7GC0-RTRMADP-3-EU-IMMIGRATION.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4f886fa4-a8eb-11f1-80af-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-04T160250Z-834668253-RC2CCNAR7GC0-RTRMADP-3-EU-IMMIGRATION.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">21af5d90-e27f-11f1-8e59-9ff547092806</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:02:50 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Comment l’Ukraine a en partie détruit le pont de Kertch en Crimée</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-comment-l-ukraine-a-en-partie-d%C3%A9truit-le-pont-de-kertch</link><description>
Cible prioritaire de l’Ukraine depuis le début de l’invasion russe, le pont de Kertch reliant la Crimée à la Russie n’est plus utilisable. Après de premières frappes lundi 16 novembre, l’armée ukrainienne a de nouveau ciblé cet ouvrage à la fois stratégique et symbolique ce mardi. Les images disponibles en sources ouvertes montrent qu’une partie importante de la section routière a été détruite.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6de17860-e284-11f1-adba-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/Russie-Ukraine-Kertch-Info-Verif-Une.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6de17860-e284-11f1-adba-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/Russie-Ukraine-Kertch-Info-Verif-Une.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">efa87d34-e285-11f1-8673-6541d1e7a339</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 13:11:05 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6de17860-e284-11f1-adba-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/Russie-Ukraine-Kertch-Info-Verif-Une.png">© Captures d'écran/ Montage RFI</source><dc:creator>Grégory Genevrier</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>«C'est un jour historique»: en Serbie, le mouvement des étudiants fait son entrée au Parlement</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-c-est-un-jour-historique-en-serbie-le-mouvement-des-%C3%A9tudiants-fait-son-entr%C3%A9e-au-parlement</link><description>
Ce mardi 17 novembre marque la première session du Parlement nouvellement élu en Serbie, qui consacre la victoire de la liste étudiante après deux ans de manifestations anticorruption.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73fb2964-e278-11f1-a3a1-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T092505Z-1014948375-RC2LPOAZ0JM3-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73fb2964-e278-11f1-a3a1-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T092505Z-1014948375-RC2LPOAZ0JM3-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c2f50a0-e279-11f1-97b9-0be1f30c0e1f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 12:33:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73fb2964-e278-11f1-a3a1-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T092505Z-1014948375-RC2LPOAZ0JM3-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg">© Zorana Jevtic / Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Soldats français déployés en Ukraine: Moscou y voit une «participation directe» au conflit</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-soldats-fran%C3%A7ais-d%C3%A9ploy%C3%A9s-en-ukraine-moscou-y-voit-une-participation-directe-au-conflit</link><description>
Ce mardi 17 novembre, le ministre russe des Affaires étrangères a qualifié de « participation directe » au conflit en Ukraine le déploiement de soldats français opérant en Ukraine pour des missions de formation et d'entretien de matériels, révélé lundi par RFI.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5112e664-3a74-11f1-904f-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26062382346034.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5112e664-3a74-11f1-904f-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26062382346034.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cc8b09f6-e277-11f1-9c03-0f08de7ca9eb</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:14:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5112e664-3a74-11f1-904f-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26062382346034.jpg">© Pavel Bednyakov/AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Appels sur l'actualité</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine : que cache la mission secrète des militaires français?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/appels-sur-l-actualit%C3%A9/20261117-guerre-en-ukraine-que-cache-la-mission-secr%C3%A8te-des-militaires-fran%C3%A7ais</link><description>
C’est une information RFI : des soldats français sont présents en Ukraine depuis l’été dernier. Selon notre enquête, ils sont réunis au sein d’un dispositif confidentiel baptisé « Volia ». Leur mission : former des militaires ukrainiens pour assurer la maintenance des équipements livrés par Paris, notamment les canons Caesar et les avions Mirage 2000. Ils ne prennent pas part aux combats. La France n’a toutefois pas confirmé officiellement l’existence de cette mission. Pourquoi cette opération n’a-t-elle pas été portée à la connaissance du Parlement ? Et comment la Russie peut-elle interpréter cette présence militaire française sur le sol ukrainien ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6edbc838-e1ad-11f1-9213-e1d07338c648</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:00:19 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juan Gomez</dc:creator></item><item><category>Appels sur l'actualité</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine : 400 000 Russes morts sur le front?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/appels-sur-l-actualit%C3%A9/20261117-guerre-en-ukraine-400-000-russes-morts-sur-le-front</link><description>
Près de 400 000 soldats russes auraient péri depuis le début de la guerre en Ukraine. C’est ce que révèlent des documents attribués à l’institut de statistiques russe Rosstat, dont deux groupes de hackers affirment avoir piraté les données. Des révélations particulièrement sensibles, alors que Vladimir Poutine a classé les informations sur les pertes militaires au secret d’État dès 2015. Comment ces hackers ont-ils pu accéder à ces données ? Ces chiffres sont-ils vraiment crédibles ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12463d34-9854-11ed-bc0b-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/AP23003562030298.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12463d34-9854-11ed-bc0b-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/AP23003562030298.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1e6ce9c6-e1ae-11f1-823e-1b46fca9b9c5</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:56:28 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juan Gomez</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Nouvel échange de frappes entre la Russie et l'Ukraine, deux morts en Crimée</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-la-russie-frappe-deux-ponts-majeurs-%C3%A0-kiev-l-ukraine-cible-%C3%A0-nouveau-la-crim%C3%A9e</link><description>
La Russie a frappé deux ponts majeurs à Kiev, et l'Ukraine a visé le pont de Crimée pour la deuxième nuit d'affilée. Ces attaques sont hautement symboliques car elles interviennent deux jours avant une rencontre en Chine entre les chefs d'État russe, américain et chinois.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/63468264-e253-11f1-9b57-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3CQ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/63468264-e253-11f1-9b57-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3CQ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">95f153a6-e253-11f1-b160-a15f137c0baa</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 06:54:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/63468264-e253-11f1-9b57-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3CQ.jpg">AFP - STRINGER</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Accents d'Europe</category><title>Sur les traces des personnes réduites en esclavage</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/accents-d-europe/20261116-sur-les-traces-des-personnes-r%C3%A9duites-en-esclavage</link><description>
Donner un nom, une histoire, à des millions d’asservis et comprendre l’impact de la traite sur les inégalités d’aujourd’hui : dans cette émission, on ouvre les registres britanniques de l’esclavage.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7ccb2-02c6-11ed-b799-005056bfa79e/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17198587355318.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7ccb2-02c6-11ed-b799-005056bfa79e/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17198587355318.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d9124e66-e1f8-11f1-bfcd-390d5e1d14eb</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 21:20:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juliette Gheerbrant</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Espagne: Lula da Silva soutient Pedro Sanchez avant les législatives anticipées du 29 novembre</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-espagne-lula-da-silva-soutient-pedro-sanchez-avant-les-l%C3%A9gislatives-anticip%C3%A9es-du-29-novembre</link><description>
Le Premier ministre espagnol Pedro Sanchez a reçu, lundi 16 novembre, le soutien du président brésilien Lula da Silva à Madrid, à moins de deux semaines des élections législatives anticipées du 29 novembre. Au pouvoir depuis 2018, le dirigeant socialiste espère inverser la tendance des sondages, qui donnent une majorité absolue aux deux partis de droite, en s'inspirant de la récente victoire de Lula lors de la dernière présidentielle au Brésil.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c241fe8-e1e7-11f1-90be-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320393432966.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c241fe8-e1e7-11f1-90be-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320393432966.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ac6cf11e-e1e8-11f1-bb05-5d0ba7174a9f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 18:53:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c241fe8-e1e7-11f1-90be-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320393432966.jpg">© AP Photo/Francisco Seco</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Soldats français en Ukraine: «Cela va sans doute amplifier la réaction de propagande de la Russie»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-soldats-fran%C3%A7ais-en-ukraine-cela-va-sans-doute-amplifier-la-r%C3%A9action-de-propagande-de-la-russie</link><description>
Comme l'a révélé RFI lundi 16 novembre, des soldats français sont en Ukraine depuis au moins l'été 2016 dans le cadre de la mission « Volia ». Ils y sont avec pour dispenser des formations et gardent un statut non belligérant dans la guerre avec la Russie. Les soldats préparent ainsi les militaires ukrainiens à l'usage d'équipements de pointe envoyés par Paris à Kiev via cette opération confidentielle qui soulage les Ukrainiens. Ulrich Bounat, chercheur associé au think tank Euro Creative et auteur de La guerre hybride en Ukraine : quelles perspectives ? (éditions du Cygne), analyse la situation.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7ddcea68-e1e1-11f1-94a2-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7BD6Z6.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7ddcea68-e1e1-11f1-94a2-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7BD6Z6.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7d03899a-e1e0-11f1-aaae-2d7f05fb51c7</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:58:48 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7ddcea68-e1e1-11f1-94a2-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7BD6Z6.jpg">AFP - THOMAS SAMSON</source><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>L'Allemagne, l'Autriche, le Danemark, la Grèce et les Pays-Bas présentent leur projet de «hub de retour» pour migrants au Rwanda</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-l-allemagne-l-autriche-le-danemark-la-gr%C3%A8ce-et-les-pays-bas-pr%C3%A9sentent-leur-projet-de-hub-de-retour-pour-migrants-au-rwanda</link><description>
Cinq pays européens défendent une politique migratoire très ferme et pilotent ensemble un projet visant à envoyer des migrants dans des centres situés hors d’Europe. Après des mois de réflexion, ils ont retenu le Rwanda pour un premier projet pilote, dont l’ouverture est prévue en 2027.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/013e2372-e1d3-11f1-80e8-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320558302536.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/013e2372-e1d3-11f1-80e8-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320558302536.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bff09a3a-e1d2-11f1-86ed-abe06ccee855</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:35:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/013e2372-e1d3-11f1-80e8-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320558302536.jpg">AP Photo/Heinz-Peter Bader - Heinz-Peter Bader</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Soldats français en Ukraine: «Nous ne sommes pas cobelligérants», rappelle le sénateur PS Rachid Temal</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261116-soldats-fran%C3%A7ais-en-ukraine-nous-ne-sommes-pas-cobellig%C3%A9rants-rappelle-le-s%C3%A9nateur-ps-rachid-temal</link><description>
Selon des informations recueillies et corroborées par RFI, des soldats français sont bien présents en Ukraine aux côtés des soldats ukrainiens pour une mission conventionnelle non combattante. Cette mission, baptisée « Volia », dure depuis au moins l'été 2026 et elle est chargée de former des combattants ukrainiens aux équipements militaires de pointe fournis par la France. Le Parlement n'a pas été consulté sur le déploiement de cette opération comme le prévoit la Constitution. Entretien avec le sénateur PS du Val-d'Oise Rachid Temal, vice-président de la Commission des affaires étrangères, de la défense et des forces armées.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/dd94df9c-ae02-11f0-a21b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/Ukraine-Soldats-Armee-Russie-Guerre.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/dd94df9c-ae02-11f0-a21b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/Ukraine-Soldats-Armee-Russie-Guerre.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dc79170e-e1c8-11f1-9f22-1b5d0dc6ca69</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:03:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Belgique: le roi Philippe accorde une semaine de plus à Bart De Wever pour boucler le budget</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-belgique-le-roi-philippe-accorde-une-semaine-de-plus-%C3%A0-bart-de-wever-pour-boucler-le-budget</link><description>
Le Premier ministre belge a dû partager le constat que les négociations sur le budget n'aboutissent toujours pas au sein de sa coalition. Le roi Philippe lui a donné, lundi 16 novembre, un nouveau délai d'une semaine, soit jusqu'au 23 novembre. Bart De Wever essaie depuis plusieurs semaines de dégager un compromis au sein de sa coalition de cinq partis sur la manière de réduire un déficit public parmi les pires de la zone euro.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fac262a6-e1c3-11f1-9dfa-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-16T103820Z-2087886533-RC2XOOA3XW4W-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-GOVERNMENT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fac262a6-e1c3-11f1-9dfa-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-16T103820Z-2087886533-RC2XOOA3XW4W-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-GOVERNMENT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2eea2d12-e1c3-11f1-bed7-13b61d5683ea</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:32:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fac262a6-e1c3-11f1-9dfa-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-16T103820Z-2087886533-RC2XOOA3XW4W-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-GOVERNMENT.jpg">REUTERS - Yves Herman</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>En Allemagne, «la réforme des services de renseignement est une révolution»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-en-allemagne-la-r%C3%A9forme-des-services-de-renseignement-est-une-r%C3%A9volution</link><description>
Vendredi 13 novembre, le Bundestag a adopté une vaste réforme renforçant les services de renseignement allemands, longtemps bridés par les héritages nazi et est-allemand, et la dépendance vis-à-vis des États-Unis. Face à la menace russe, Berlin entend désormais combler son retard et peser davantage sur la scène internationale. Un tournant majeur décrypté par Joachim Bitterlich, ancien conseiller du chancelier allemand Helmut Kohl sur les affaires européennes et de sécurité.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/81eb9b82-e06e-11f1-a32c-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26280291105956.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/81eb9b82-e06e-11f1-a32c-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26280291105956.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec11b566-e049-11f1-a0f7-b9a889b5d5a2</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:57:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/81eb9b82-e06e-11f1-a32c-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26280291105956.jpg">© Markus Schreiber / AP Photo</source><dc:creator>Christophe Drevet</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Les affaires de violences sexuelles impliquant Russell Brand et David Walliams secouent le Royaume-Uni</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-les-affaires-de-violences-sexuelles-impliquant-russell-brand-et-david-walliams-secouent-le-royaume-uni</link><description>
Au Royaume-Uni, deux visages, ceux de Russell Brand et de David Walliams, deux comédiens très célèbres outre-Manche, qui ont notamment travaillé à la BBC, sont impliqués dans affaires de violences sexistes et sexuelles. Ils auraient tous les deux profité de leur statut pour agir en toute impunité. Russell Brand vient d’être condamné à 10 ans et demi de prison, jugé coupable d’un viol et de trois agressions sexuelles. Le second, David Walliams, est accusé de viols et d’abus sexuels.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c904996-e19e-11f1-8640-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26315367622643.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c904996-e19e-11f1-8640-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26315367622643.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f805e7f2-e198-11f1-ab18-c7cd260b5a64</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:39:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c904996-e19e-11f1-8640-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26315367622643.jpg">AP Photo/Kin Cheung, Ki Price - Kin Cheung, Ki Price</source><dc:creator>Emeline Vin</dc:creator></item><item><category>Appels sur l'actualité</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine : l'Europe sera-t-elle enfin à la table des négociations?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/appels-sur-l-actualit%C3%A9/20261116-guerre-en-ukraine-l-europe-sera-t-elle-enfin-%C3%A0-la-table-des-n%C3%A9gociations</link><description>
L'Allemagne, la France, l’Italie, la Pologne et le Royaume-Uni pourraient rejoindre les prochaines négociations entre l’Ukraine et la Russie. C’est, en tout cas, ce qu’assurent les émissaires américains Jared Kushner et Steve Witkoff qui affirment que Vladimir Poutine a donné son accord à la présence des Européens. Mais à Moscou, aucune confirmation pour l’instant. Comment expliquer ces déclarations ? S’agit-il d’une réelle ouverture de la Russie ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2c77cbc6-df24-11f1-a56b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316808764019.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2c77cbc6-df24-11f1-a56b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316808764019.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0e291278-df61-11f1-9ecc-33767f4b6941</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:05:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juan Gomez</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>L'Ukraine frappe le pont reliant la Russie à la Crimée annexée par Moscou</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-l-ukraine-frappe-le-pont-reliant-la-russie-%C3%A0-la-crim%C3%A9e-annex%C3%A9e-par-moscou</link><description>
L'Ukraine a « frappé » le pont reliant la Russie à la péninsule de Crimée annexée par Moscou en 2014, restreignant la circulation sur cet ouvrage stratégique, a annoncé lundi 16 novembre le chef des autorités locales nommé par Moscou.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/e6618ed8-e18f-11f1-a857-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3ZQ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/e6618ed8-e18f-11f1-a857-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3ZQ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1f94f66c-e191-11f1-95aa-5b9e7bed2e56</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 07:42:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/e6618ed8-e18f-11f1-a857-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3ZQ.jpg">© AFP - STRINGER</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Mission «Volia»: comment l'armée française opère en Ukraine</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-mission-volia-comment-l-arm%C3%A9e-fran%C3%A7aise-op%C3%A8re-en-ukraine</link><description>
Paris n'a jamais confirmé la présence de militaires français sur le sol ukrainien. Or, selon plusieurs interlocuteurs joints par RFI, un soutien militaire français joue un rôle actif dans le pays depuis au moins l'été 2026.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6fc6cbc2-e012-11f1-96bb-d5c8a7614a7b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 04:59:35 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg">AFP - MARTIN BUREAU</source><dc:creator>Franck Alexandre</dc:creator></item><item><category>Reportage international</category><title>Au Royaume-Uni, des archives inédites pour retrouver les ancêtres victimes de l'esclavage</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/reportage-international/20261115-au-royaume-uni-des-archives-in%C3%A9dites-pour-retrouver-les-anc%C3%AAtres-victimes-de-l-esclavage</link><description>
À Londres, au Royaume-Uni, des universités ont compilé et mis en ligne des archives pour créer un registre des personnes réduites en esclavage par les Britanniques dans leurs colonies, jusqu'au XIXe siècle. Jusqu'à présent, les registres disponibles identifiaient les propriétaires de plantations et de personnes asservies. C'est la première fois que sont rassemblées et publiées des informations détaillées sur les victimes de la traite transatlantique. Ces archives sont exceptionnelles : elles représentent une source précieuse pour les historiens, mais aussi pour tous les descendants qui cherchent à connaître leurs ancêtres et leur histoire.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8857c74-6ca9-11f1-9b88-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-972Z7PA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8857c74-6ca9-11f1-9b88-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-972Z7PA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">580fc43e-e12a-11f1-accf-5ba32673de97</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 23:02:19 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marie Billon</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>
